LTV Increment Flow

7 core emails + 1 SMS + ongoing monthly follow up.

First cycle starts Day 21 after delivery. After 2 orders, timing shifts to the clinic's own observed gap between orders.

Emails 1 to 3 are restock. Emails 4 to 7 are reactivation. Emails 5, 6 and 7 all lead with the 25 unit threshold.

EMAIL 3 — USE THE THRESHOLD FOR THIS RESTOCK

Subject {{units_to_25}} units changes the restock

Preview Mix the order however you like.

Plain text. 6 days after Email 1, when no reorder has happened and the threshold is relevant. Suppress if the last order was 25 units or more.

Option A25 unit grid

Restock bigger than last time.

Your last order was {{last_order_qty}} units on {{last_order_date}}. Wholesale pricing starts at 25 units in a single order.

That puts you {{units_to_25}} units away, and the units do not have to be the same item.

Review restock options

  • Same compound, more of it. The straightforward route if your usage is steady.

  • Different compounds on the same order. Anything in the catalogue counts toward the 25.

  • A larger format. Fewer lines to reach the same count.

  • An approved blend. GLOW, KLOW, WOLVERINE and the 2X blends sit in the catalogue the same way the single compounds do.

A restock is the easiest order to consolidate, because you are already placing it. Pulling next quarter's line onto this one costs you nothing in shipping and crosses the threshold on the whole order rather than the line.

Your account pricing is in the portal.

EMAIL 5 — COMPARE THE COA

Subject Put the two COAs side by side

Preview {{units_to_25}} units from wholesale, and one thing worth checking.

Designed. 3 days after Email 4. Leads with the threshold, then invites a documentation comparison. Needs Parth's sign off before it ships.

Option ATwo documents on a surface

{{units_to_25}} units from wholesale.

Wholesale starts at 25 units in one order, and they do not have to be the same item.

Review the threshold

That is the commercial part. Here is the other part.

If you are buying this compound somewhere else now, that is a reasonable thing to have done. The only thing worth doing before it becomes permanent is putting the two documents next to each other.

Ask for the COA on the exact lot you received

Not a representative COA. Not last quarter's. The document for the lot number printed on the vial in your fridge. If those two numbers do not match, there is nothing to compare.

Count the tests on it

Ours runs 11: conformity, identity, purity, net content, endotoxins, sterility, total yeast and mold, heavy metals, residual solvents, pH and water activity.

Check what purity is measured against

Ours is ≥99% with the measured figure printed per lot, not a catalogue claim applied to everything.

Check whether there was a hold

A lot that ships the day it is made has not been tested on the material that shipped.

We are not telling you what you will find. We are telling you what to look at. If the other document holds up, you have made a good decision with evidence behind it.

View a Frontier COA

Option ASeven glass bubbles

Which one is it?

You ordered {{last_order_qty}} units of {{compound}} on {{last_order_date}} and nothing since.

Before anything else: wholesale starts at 25 units in one order and they do not have to be the same item, which puts you {{units_to_25}} units away.

If the reason you have not ordered is not pricing, reply with one letter and we will do the matching thing:

  • A.

    We have enough stock. We push the reminders back to match your real cycle.

  • B.

    We switched suppliers. We send the documentation comparison and leave the decision with you.

  • C.

    Pricing. We show you where the threshold lands for your volume and route it to someone who can talk about larger requirements.

  • D.

    Availability. We send current lot and inventory information on the items you buy.

  • E.

    We need a different product. We point you at the right part of the catalogue.

  • F.

    We are ordering less. We cut the cadence rather than keep the account on a schedule it has outgrown.

  • G.

    Something else. A person follows up and you tell them.

Reply with your letter

One letter is a complete reply. You do not need to write a sentence.

3 emails. Trigger: a new compound becomes available in the Frontier portal.

Email 1 same day or next business day, Email 2 at +2 days, Email 3 at +2 days after that.

EMAIL 1 — NEW IN FRONTIER: {{COMPOUND}}

Subject New in the portal: {{compound}}

Preview Sizes, lot and COA inside.

Designed. Same day or next business day after portal release.

Option AFull size set in a row

{{compound}} is in the catalogue.

Available in {{sizes_available}}. Shipping from lot {{lot}}.

View {{compound}}

New catalogue item, live in the portal as of today. Here is everything we can tell you about it, which is everything that matters operationally:

The name on the label

{{compound}}, exactly as it appears in the portal. No house naming, no proprietary rebadging of a compound you already know by another name.

The formats

{{sizes_available}}. Sterile multiple dose vials, same as the rest of the catalogue.

The lot and the panel
